The same early-1900s Liberty villa above the centro of Anghiari, established from the listings' own text rather than photographs — both describe a villa built for a wealthy Briton, a 2.600 m² park with statues, years of use as an art gallery, Impruneta terracotta floors and pietra serena door surrounds. They share NO photographs at all (best hamming 17), which is worth recording: a non-match proves nothing. Both ask € 1.600.000; Lionard says 550 m², Romolini 490 m². Leonardi lists it too at € 2.900.000, but that listing was last updated in December 2020 and offers the sale combined with a second building in the same park, so its price is not comparable and is excluded rather than published as an 81% gap.
Same interior — identical photograph of the beamed staircase and kitchen (Marcellini watermark). Leonardi says 400 m², Marcellini 200 m²; neither publishes a price.

One property listed three times under the Cortesi brand — same stone room with blue floor, same aerial. € 80.000 throughout; 87 m² or 105 m²; rustico or villa.

Villa Colcello at Monterchi, established from both listings' text: same Strada Vicinale del Colcello, two independent apartments one per floor, pool, land. The same house on the old walls of Anghiari's centro storico, at € 325.000 with 5+ rooms and 3+ bathrooms on both. Tiberimmobiliare files it as an appartamento while its own description calls it a 'terra tetto'; Romolini files it as a cieloterra. 150 vs 170 m².

The same restored villa with pool near Monterchi at € 890.000. Cortesi puts the main residence at 340 m² with 5 bedrooms and 3 bathrooms; Romolini gives the same 5-and-3 for a main villa of 205 m², a headline of 300 m², and a 14 × 7 m pool. The disagreement is over the building, not the property.

The same restored casale near Anghiari at € 899.000. Romolini's own arithmetic explains the gap: house 305 m² plus a converted fienile of 43 m² = 348 m², while Now Immobilare publishes 309 m² — the disagreement is whether the barn counts.
The same second-floor flat on Via Tiberina Sud, Sansepolcro, at € 130.000 — both describe a small palazzina, two bathrooms and a garage. 135 vs 150 m².

The same raised-ground-floor flat on Via Fausto Vagnetti, Anghiari, at € 190.000: small hillside condominio, panoramic, eat-in kitchen, two bathrooms. Tiberimmobiliare says 103 m², R.E.Volution's field says 93 m² and its own text says 90 m².

The same house near the centre of Sansepolcro at € 260.000, with matching floor-by-floor layouts, garden and garage. Cortesi calls it a casa SINGOLA of 200 m²; Leonardi calls it a casa BIFAMILIARE, free on three sides, of 211 m² — detached or semi-detached is not a matter of wording.

La Scheggia, Anghiari: three flats at € 145.000 in the SAME converted casa colonica of four units, not one property listed three times. itcasa's 'Appartamento Menta' is explicitly on the first floor; the other two are on the second. A building split into equally priced units is a false-positive class the price+surface route cannot see, and the only tell was in the listing text.

Both are € 105.000 to-renovate properties with a garden in the Sansepolcro periferia, at about 115–130 m². But Marcellini describes a rural building with a seccatoio and 4.000 m² of land, while SICASA describes a flat with its own entrance inside a trifamiliare on Via del Tevere. A rural building divided into three units would reconcile them; nothing in either listing settles it.

Both are € 149.000 flats of 110–115 m² on the second floor of a historic palazzo on Via XX Settembre, Sansepolcro, with one bathroom — but the room counts differ (5 vs 3) and a palazzo storico holds several flats. La Scheggia is the cautionary case: same building, same price, different units. Not publishable on this evidence. (Noted in passing: SICASA's floor FIELD says 3° while its own description says 'piano secondo'.)

Via Casa al Vento: the three Leonardi listings are joined only by an identical photograph of the LAKE VIEW (hamming 0) — the same panorama from three different houses in the same hillside, not one property; their surfaces run 200 to 420 m². The Marcellini join is a bedroom against a kitchen. Note the furniture guard did not catch the view because it appears in exactly three listings and the rule drops images appearing in MORE than three; lowering that threshold would destroy real three-agency clusters, so this is a case for the verified overlay, not a tuning change.
Corso Matteotti 'triple': the photo joins (hamming 7-10) match a kitchen to a bathroom and the bathroom to a hallway. Three different flats on three different streets in two comuni.
Via del Garbo: hall vs staircase vs corridor, all different rooms (hamming 7-10). Includes the intra-Centogambe pair.
